title: Chicken Paella
subtitle: Simple family version
ingredients: 6 small chicken legs or 4 small thighs
method: Heat a good splash of olive oil in the pan on high heat.
Season the chicken with salt and brown it well on all sides on high heat.
Add the green beans and cook on high heat until softened and slightly browned.
Add the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds (do not let it burn), then add the tomato. Cook on medium heat until the tomato breaks down.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the water and crumble in the stock cube. Stir once and spread everything evenly.
Do not stir again once the rice is cooking.
Cook on medium heat until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Place the rosemary on top.
Lower the heat, cover with a lid, and cook until the rice is done.
Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: If the rice is still hard and the pan is dry, add a little more water.
Do not keep stirring or the rice will not cook properly.
A slightly crispy bottom is good, but do not let it burn.
notes: This recipe is adapted from the video How To Make Spanish Paella | Omar Allibhoy.

title: Granny’s Soup
subtitle: Simple chicken stock vegetable soup
ingredients: 1.5 litres chicken stock (or water with stock cubes)
method: Slice the spring onions, carrots, celery and leek.
Chop the parsley.
Bring the stock to the boil in a large pan.
Add the vegetables and bring back to the boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 30 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Add the parsley for the last few minutes.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
tips: Cut the carrots fairly small so they cook in time.
If using stock cubes, make the stock first before adding vegetables.
notes: You can leave out celery or leek, but not both or the soup loses flavour.
Quantities do not need to be exact.
If you keep it out of the fridge, you need to boil it every day.

title: Sopa de Lentejas
subtitle: Colombian lentil and potato soup
method: Add the carrots, lentils, water, stock cubes and cumin to a large pot.
Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer.
Cook until the lentils are nearly soft.
Add the potatoes and continue cooking for 15–30 minutes until tender.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper before serving.
Serve with coriander on top.
tips: If the soup gets too thick, add a little more water.
This is often better the next day.
notes: For extra flavour, fry chopped bacon first, then add the rest of the ingredients.
You can also add chopped sausages instead.

title: Caldito
subtitle: Colombian chicken and potato soup
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts (on the bone if possible)
500g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
method: Put the chicken, water, cumin, salt and pepper into a large pot.
Tie the spring onions and one pack of coriander together and add to the pot.
Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for about 25 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot.
Add a stock cube if needed and stir.
Add the potatoes.
While the potatoes are cooking, take the meat off the bone and pull it apart into small pieces using two forks.
Cook the potatoes for 15–20 minutes until soft.
Remove and discard the tied herbs.
Serve the soup and place the chicken pieces on top.
Add chopped fresh coriander (second pack) before serving.
tips: Taste the broth after removing the chicken and adjust stock if needed.
Pulling the chicken apart with forks gives a better texture than cutting it.
notes: Serving the chicken on top keeps it from overcooking.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
subtitle: Classic mince and mashed potato dish
method: Slice the onion and cook in butter or oil with a little salt until soft.
Add the minced beef and cook until browned.
Add Worcestershire sauce and pepper.
Cook the frozen vegetables separately in boiling water, then drain.
Add the vegetables to the meat and mix.
Pour into an oven dish and spread out evenly.
Spoon the tomatoes over the top.
Peel and boil the potatoes until soft, then drain.
Mash with butter and a little milk.
Spread the mashed potato over the meat.
Sprinkle grated cheese on top.
Bake at 180°C until the top is golden (about 45–60 minutes).
tips: Let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
Make extra and freeze one portion.
notes: You can add crushed crisps on top for extra crunch.

title: Slow-cooked Lamb with Green Lentils
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb with lentils, tomatoes and mint
ingredients: 1.5–1.8kg shoulder or leg of lamb (on the bone or boned, both fine)
half a jar of sun-dried tomatoes, cut into halves or quarters
method: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Season the lamb with salt and pepper.
Scatter the onion in the bottom of the casserole dish and put the lamb on top.
Add the garlic, oregano, lemon juice, olive oil and wine.
Cover with the lid and cook for 30 minutes.
Remove from the oven and add the lentils, water, tomatoes and mint.
Stir everything around the lamb.
Cover again and return to the oven at 150°C.
Cook for about 3 hours, until the lamb is very tender.
Remove the lamb and cut or pull it into pieces.
Serve the lamb with the lentils spooned around it.
tips: Check from time to time that there is enough liquid in the casserole.
If it looks too dry, add a little water.
This works well with either shoulder or leg.
notes: You can use Puy or green lentils lentils.

title: Thai Chicken Tom Yum
subtitle: Hot and sour chicken soup
method: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and cook for a few minutes until starting to soften.
Add the stock, mushrooms, lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, chilli and fish sauce.
Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and green beans and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat.
Stir in the lime juice.
Taste and add salt if needed.
Serve and garnish with chopped coriander.
tips: Do not eat the lime leaves, galangal or lemongrass pieces.
If you want it less spicy, use less chilli.
Add the lime juice at the end so it keeps its sharp flavour.
notes: The herbs (lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves) are usually kept in the freezer.
Serve with noodles or rice for a main course.

title: Piquant Tomato Soup
subtitle: Smooth tomato soup with a slightly sharp flavour
ingredients: 1 tin whole plum tomatoes with their juice
1 litre stock, made with cubes if needed
method: Melt the margarine or butter in a large saucepan over low heat.
Add the onion, carrot and celery.
Cover and cook gently for about 10 minutes until softened, without browning.
Add all the remaining ingredients.
Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for about 45 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Remove the bay leaf and lemon peel.
Blend until smooth.
Return to the pan, heat through and serve.
tips: Keep the vegetables gentle at the start. Do not let them brown.
Blend carefully while hot.
Add a little water or stock if it feels too thick after blending.
notes: You do not use the optional thickening or vermicelli from the original recipe.

title: Granny’s Red Cabbage
subtitle: Sweet and sharp red cabbage with apple
ingredients: 4 tablespoons red or white wine vinegar
method: Melt the margarine in a large saucepan.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage and apples and cook gently for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the cloves, vinegar, water, sugar, salt and pepper.
Bring to the boil.
Lower the heat, cover and cook for 1 to 2 hours until the cabbage is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
tips: Stir it occasionally so it does not catch.
The cabbage should be soft, not watery.
This freezes well.
notes: Granny Smith apples work well where cooking apples are not available.
This can also be cooked in the microwave.

title: Apple Strudel
subtitle: Puff pastry apple strudel
ingredients: extra Demerara sugar for the top
method: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Roll out the pastry into 2 rectangles.
Mix the sugar, ground almonds, cinnamon and raisins together.
Spread some of the mixture in a line down the middle of each pastry rectangle.
Peel and core the apples.
Cut the apples into pieces and place them on top of the mixture.
Sprinkle the rest of the sugar mixture over the apples.
Moisten the edges of the pastry with water.
Fold one long side over the filling, then fold the other side over and press to seal.
Fold in the ends and press them closed.
Moisten the top and sprinkle Demerara sugar over it.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until golden.
tips: Do not overfill or it becomes harder to seal.
Serve warm or cold.
This amount makes 2 strudels.
notes: Granny Smith apples work well where cooking apples are not available.
Ground almonds help absorb juice from the apples.

title: Cheese Cake
subtitle: Classic baked cheesecake with sour cream topping
equipment: 7–8 inch round cake tin (loose bottom if possible)
method: Heat the oven to 160°C.
Melt the butter and mix with the biscuit crumbs.
Press into the base of the tin.
Mix the cheese, sugar and vanilla.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing between each.
Pour into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes.
Turn off the oven, open the door slightly and leave to cool inside.
Remove from oven once cool.
Increase oven to 180°C.
Mix the sour cream, sugar and vanilla.
Spread over the cake.
Return to the oven for 5 minutes.
Cool and refrigerate.
tips: Do not rush the cooling stage or it may crack.
Best made the day before.
notes: Use a loose-bottom tin if possible.

title: Abue’s Arroz de Leche
subtitle: Creamy rice pudding with coconut and spices
ingredients: 1 egg yolk, mixed with a little milk
method: Heat the coconut milk, cinnamon, star anise and butter.
Just before boiling, add the washed rice.
Cook on medium heat, stirring regularly.
As it absorbs liquid, add milk gradually.
Continue until rice is fully cooked and creamy.
Add condensed milk to taste.
Stir in the egg yolk mixture continuously.
Add vodka or aguardiente and turn off heat.
Leave on warm hob briefly, stirring.
Cool, stirring occasionally.
Add milk if too thick when cold.
tips: Stir regularly to prevent sticking.
Add milk gradually, not all at once.
It thickens as it cools.
notes: Add more milk if it becomes too thick.

title: Thai Green Curry
subtitle: Simple chicken green curry
method: Heat oil in a pan or wok.
Add curry paste and cook for 1–2 minutes.
Add chicken and coat well.
Add coconut milk and stock.
Add green beans and fish sauce.
Add lime leaves if using.
Simmer 8–10 minutes until chicken is cooked.
Add optional vegetables if using.
Remove from heat and add Thai basil.
tips: Adjust curry paste for spice level.
Do not overcook the chicken.
notes: Kaffir lime leaves are usually kept in the freezer.
If the curry needs more liquid, add more stock.

title: Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
subtitle: Simple meatballs with fresh tomato sauce
method: Cut tomatoes into chunks.
Heat oil and brown meatballs (5–7 minutes).
Remove and set aside.
Cook onion until soft.
Add garlic briefly.
Add tomatoes and seasoning.
Add wine or balsamic if using.
Cook 10–15 minutes, breaking tomatoes down.
Add water if needed.
Return meatballs.
Cover and cook 15–20 minutes.
Adjust seasoning.
tips: Browning adds most of the flavour.
Reduce uncovered if too watery.
notes: Tomate chucha is watery so allow time to reduce.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
subtitle: Quick chicken stir-fry with vegetables
method: Prepare everything before starting.
Heat oil on high.
Cook chicken about 5 minutes.
Push aside or remove.
Cook onion 2–3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger briefly.
Add green beans 3–4 minutes.
Add cabbage 2–3 minutes.
Return chicken.
Add soy sauce and pepper.
Cook 2–3 minutes and serve.
tips: Keep heat high throughout.
Do not overcrowd the pan.
notes: Serve with rice or noodles.
You can add hoisin or oyster sauce for variation.
